case_name: M.M. Cooperative Bank Limited v J.P. Bhimani And Another
respondent:
J.P. Bhimani And Another
Supreme Court of India

31 July 2009
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1374 OF 2009 (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.4129 of 2004)
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.
1.  Appellant-Madhavpura Mercantile Cooperative Bank Ltd. (the bank) is a banking organization incorporated and registered under the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act. It is now under a reconstruction scheme as contemplated by Section 15(b) of the Multi State Cooperative Societies Act, 1984 (for short, the '1984 Act') since repealed and replaced by the Multi State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. The said reconstruction scheme was framed as directed by the Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Agriculture and Cooperation of the Government of India.

facts: Appellant-Madhavpura Mercantile Cooperative Bank Ltd. is a banking organization incorporated and registered under the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act.
The bank at present is managed by a Board of Management constituted in terms of the said scheme.

A criminal complaint registered as C.R.8 of 2003 was filed, inter alia, against the respondents alleging siphoning of the funds by the accused in conspiracy with each other and, thus, they are said to have committed offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420, 467, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.
The amount involved in the aforementioned complaint is said to be Rs.8 crores.
issues: Whether the High Court committed a serious error in releasing the first respondent on bail
Whether the total amount involved in the scam is huge and should be taken into consideration
petitioner_arguments: The High Court failed to take into consideration that as the total amount involved in the scam is huge viz. to the tune of 107 crores of rupees.
In any event, keeping in view the offer made by the appellant, he should at least be directed to pay a sum of Rs.41 crores.
respondent_arguments: The respondent had been granted bail after remaining behind the bar for about eight months.
Even if the advances to the other concerns of the respondents are taken into consideration, the same would come to Rs.23.84 crores
The respondent No.1 had made payments in terms of the directions of the High Court.
court_reasoning: The learned advocate Mr. Lakhani appearing for the applicant submitted that a picture is sought to be drawn by the prosecution that the applicant has been transacting the bank since 1977 and has indulged in irregular transactions from the beginning throughout the period but the fact is otherwise
Mr. Lakhani submitted that the applicant is a businessman and a regular loanee of the Bank.
He has been regulating repaying the dues to the bank.
holding: The High Court's order granting bail to the first respondent was upheld
